page: Amazon Web Services c7g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 64 vCPUs mapped directly to 64 physical execution units. Memory configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 compute-optimized core-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per core. Local NVMe storage is not bundled, requiring external network block storage for persistence. Network interfaces feature a baseline throughput of 30 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across highly parallel execution pipelines. The 64 dedicated cores produce top-tier Clang software compilation throughput alongside top 25% results in multi-core Geekbench (20,590.0) and multi-core stress-ng (97,859.32). Memory subsystem metrics place PassMark memory testing in the top 10%, supported by 276.15 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 120.86 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth. Network-adjacent tests also show high capability, achieving 100.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 71.89 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within average ranges, recording 1,533.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1,531.49 in stress-ng single-core tests.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the ARMv8 instruction set and memory ratio. The Neoverse-V1 core omits standard x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, relying instead on native ARM cryptographic acceleration (AES enabled). Single-threaded LLM generation speeds for tiny 135M models trail in the bottom 25% at 64.46 tokens/sec, though medium 7B model generation reaches the top 25% at 31.32 tokens/sec. Without local disks, all persistent state relies on remote network block storage.

The qualitative cost profile is well matched to workloads requiring consistent dedicated compute cycles rather than burst capacity. The absence of hyperthreading eliminates resource contention between threads, making the c7g.16xlarge an efficient platform for large-scale CI/CD build farms, batch processing, static web serving clusters, Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency microservices.

Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it allocates one physical core per vCPU and 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance shows strong multi-threaded execution, placing software compilation in the top 10% and multi-core CPU testing in the top 25%, alongside 100.88 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include moderate single-thread scores and the absence of x86 vector extensions. This server is best suited for parallel software compilation, distributed caching, containerized web serving, and compute-intensive batch processing.
